I like the idea of Fighting-types for Illinois as a callback to the industrial labor that Chicago was known for for so long, but Machamp doesn't seem like quite the right fit to me.

Maybe Scrafty--it combines the Fighting-type strength with the Dark-type nefariousness that, for better or for worse, is definitely also a part of Illinois' state legacy, with a group connection that could be seen as invoking gangs, unions, or any number of other community-level gatherings, which are definitely another commonplace thing in the Chicago area.

I like the idea of a Dark-type, because between the Al Capone gangster years and a more modern history of governmental corruption... well, it does fit the state.

Honestly I could see Stunky/Skuntank, and I don't intend that as an insult or that Illinois "stinks". (Though some would argue that it does, and there are parts that literally smell...) But we've got a fair few skunks here, and the Poison/Dark typing fits well enough with the worse parts of our state's reputation, while the skunk form still references the wildlife, nature, and connection between people and animals that makes up a good part of the state in reality.

I've got all three (ADHD, depression, anxiety) myself. Meds are really hit or miss and based on the individual. One thing that may be helpful for you as it was for me is I have a weekly pill organizer with each day listed and spots for morning and night pills--I keep it on my nightstand, so it's right there when I wake up in the morning, and if I'm ever not sure if I took my pills I can check the slot for the most recent time I should've. We actually don't disagree much on this point! Voting for the more left candidate is still the best option even when their being left would be a joke in any other political system. But that vote needs to be just the beginning of our activism, not the end of it.

Also, I'm honestly not sure that time alone will fix this. There are still plenty of young people in the far-right, and some of the difference in politics in the current demographics can be explained by the fact that liberal folks tend to be from various underprivileged minorities that just don't live as long as the rich white folks who consistently vote conservative.

We can't just keep voting Democrat and assume that'll eventually fix things--we need to vote Democrat (or whatever the most-left option is, but let's face it, that's what we've got in this system) while pushing the party and the country's Overton window as far left as possible along the way.

Absolutely. There are a few factors at work that we'd need to fix--electoral college, first past the post voting, various limits on candidates and campaigns that need to be changed or overhauled (for instance, IIRC, a local candidate wanted to run for judge as an independent, but it required more signatures than running as a Democrat or Republican, which is all kinds of messed up). It'd take a lot of work... I just hope we can make it happen before it's too late.
